fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`7e9e-07f7-8fe1-4e38` delivered gateway correlation headers but explicitly deferred the
run-level root span. The consequence is stated in that epic's Out-of-scope and is real: rebar
opens no span per gate run, so `tracing.py`'s per-candidate spans are each their own trace root.
A plan-review that fans out across chunk, container and verify calls therefore appears in
Langfuse as many traces rather than one, and the gateway header id (minted at the boundary when
nothing is recording) does not match any of them.

Prior-art review of the header design flagged this as the idiomatic end state — Langfuse's own
model is one trace per unit of work — and the epic's own plan-review confirmed the shipped
behaviour does not achieve it.

## Approach

Open one rebar-owned span at each gate run boundary in `workflow/gate_dispatch.py`, so every
agent call in the run nests beneath it and the run is one trace.
`run_identity.mint_run_identity` already prefers an active recording span's trace id over
minting, so the correlation header and the exported spans then carry the same value with no
further change — that read exists precisely to make this cheap.

**The span must ENCLOSE the `gate_config(...)` statement, not sit inside it.** Both sites read
`gate_config(with_identity(cfg, ...))` (`:174`, `:706`), and `with_identity` is evaluated as an
ARGUMENT — it runs before the `with` body opens. A span opened inside that block would therefore
not be the active recording span when `mint_run_identity` fires, and it would mint anyway,
silently defeating the whole change. This ordering is the load-bearing fact.

**Three boundaries, not two.** `produce_code_review_verdict` (`:372`) is the third gate-run
boundary, with its own multi-pass fan-out whose per-candidate spans are equally separate trace
roots. It is IN scope: it opens no `gate_config`/`with_identity`, so it gains the one-trace-
per-run grouping but not header correlation — which is the right outcome, since `review-code`
has no ticket and its `${run:...}` headers are omitted by design.

Contextvar propagation into the parallel fan-out already works (`generation._submit_ctx` runs
each pool task under `copy_context()`), so no threading work is required.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — open the run span ENCLOSING all three
  boundaries (`:174` plan-review, `:706` completion, `:372` code-review).
- `src/rebar/llm/tracing.py` — the span factory, alongside the existing `candidate_span`.
- `tests/unit/test_run_span.py` (new).

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests against the real tracer — span parentage runs for real in-process.

- Happy path: candidate spans opened inside a gate run share the run span's trace id.
- Parallel path: a candidate span opened inside a `_submit_ctx`-submitted pool task shares it
  too — the fan-out is the whole point, so a main-context-only assertion proves nothing.
- Edge: with no tracer configured, behaviour is unchanged and nothing raises.
- Correlation: `mint_run_identity` inside the run returns the run span's trace id, so the
  gateway header and the exported spans agree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two candidate spans opened within one gate run share a trace id; checked by asserting both
      against the run span's context.
- [ ] A candidate span opened INSIDE a `generation._submit_ctx` pool task shares the run span's
      trace id; checked by submitting the span-opening work through the real `_submit_ctx` and
      comparing. This is the load-bearing case: the criterion above passes even if both spans
      open on the main context, leaving the parallel-propagation path — which is the entire
      reason a fanned-out run is currently many traces — unexercised.
- [ ] Inside a gate run with a recording tracer, `mint_run_identity` returns that run span's
      trace id rather than a minted value — the assertion that fails if the span is opened
      inside rather than around the `gate_config(with_identity(...))` statement.
- [ ] A code-review run's candidate spans share one trace id; checked by asserting two of them
      against each other, proving the third boundary is covered.
- [ ] With no tracer configured the gate run behaves exactly as before; checked by asserting no
      exception and an unchanged verdict shape.
- [ ] `gate_dispatch.py` stays at or under the 800-line module cap.
